findings.F1: In falling markets (60-day return below -10 %), the next day after an up day weakens as the range widens against the 20-day mean range: next-day unusual move -0.40 % (range under 1x, 896 cases, 262 days), -0.68 % (1 to 1.5x, 251 cases), -0.86 % (1.5 to 2.2x, 113 cases) and -3.04 % (above 2.2x, 36 cases, 24 days, t -2.79). Rising markets show no such fade: +2.07 % after their widest up days (116 cases, t 1.42).
findings.F2: Across all 1,296 up days in falling markets, the next-day unusual move rises with the day's 5-day return (Spearman +0.117, p < 0.0001): the further the coin is still down over 5 days, the larger the next-day fall. The same correlation is -0.020 (p 0.65, 503 days) in choppy markets and -0.002 (p 0.93, 1,386 days) in rising ones, so the gradient lives only in falling markets and needs no wide range.
findings.F3: Range width also grades next days across all falling-market up days (Spearman -0.089, p 0.0014, 1,296 cases), but not in choppy (-0.043, p 0.33) or rising markets (+0.011, p 0.68). The close's place in the range does not grade them (Spearman +0.007, p 0.80).
findings.F4: The fade after a falling-market wide up day is a one-day move, partly given back afterwards: day 1 -1.39 % (t -2.08, 149 cases, 79 days), day 2 +0.97 % (t 1.93), day 3 -0.67 % (t -1.00).
findings.F5: Among falling-market wide up days, the cases that close in the top quarter and are still down over 5 days carry the fade: -3.51 % (t -2.40, 26 cases, 13 days). The same days with a positive 5-day return give only -0.51 % (t -0.58, 65 cases).
findings.F6: The book's profit rests on very few days. It is active on 64 coin-days, wins on only 34 % of them, averages +0.85 % per active day, and its 5 best days make 54 % of its summed gain. Thin activity, not a small move, is what fails Calmar and trades per day.
findings.F7: Other angles showed nothing that stands out after this many cuts. Weekday unusual moves stay within t ±1.5. Large down days rebound (z -3 to -2: +1.10 %, t 2.05; wide low-close down days in rising markets: +1.98 %, t 2.23), but the map already holds this many times over on the long side.

ideas.idea: In a falling market, an up day is followed by a fall over the next day, larger the more the coin is still down over its 5-day return including that day, whatever the width of the day's range.
ideas.consequence: In a downtrend, a trader can sell for one day into any up day that leaves the coin below where it was 5 days ago, and sell more the deeper that 5-day loss, which gives far more cases than wide days alone.
ideas.name: falling market still-down bounce fade

ideas.idea: In a falling market, an up day is followed by a fall over the next day, larger the wider its high-to-low range against the coin's average daily range over the past 20 days and the more the coin is still down over its 5-day return including that day.
ideas.consequence: In a downtrend, a trader can short every up day for one day, sized up both by how wide it was and by how far the coin still sits below its level of 5 days ago, with no need for a close near the high.
ideas.name: width and depth bounce fade
